analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence | Morning Briefing (October 22, 2026)
key_insights: Futures are sharply lower pre-market: SPX -1.1%, NDX -1.9%, RTY -0.9%. Tech leads the decline as the tech selloff resumes. WTI is +238bps at $99.46, gold -135bps at $4,085, silver -353bps at $55.92, the 10Y is at 5.071% and VIX is at 18.49.

The headline catalyst is an NYT report that the US and Israel are drawing up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the US mid-term election, which pushed oil up 2-3%. JPM's desk says the underlying driver is still unresolved concern over how AI spending is financed, plus a lack of conviction or re-grossing after the recent tech reversal.
META reversed an initial post-earnings gain of over +5% to about -2% pre-market. TSLA is -5.2% and NVDA -2.4% pre-market.

Treasury yields are down about 3-5bp across the curve (bull steepening) in a flight-to-quality move, helped by another spike in French 10-year yields. The dollar is softer, with DXY about -22bp. Cyclicals sold off broadly and defensives outperformed.

Europe is in broad de-risking. SX5E is -1.8%, SXXP -1.1%, DAX -1.0% and UKX -0.6%. Semis and Electrification are among the worst baskets, while Defensives and Rate-sensitive baskets are the only ones up. France is the stress point, with 10Y yields +11bp to 5.12%, a fresh high in risk premium. Bunds are -2bp and Gilts -1bp. Asia: HSI -3.0%, NKY -2.7%, KOSPI -3.5%, CSI -1.8%.
Wednesday's session closed near its highs, led by AI/Tech and Momentum, with machinery, banks, credit cards and hotels also rallying. That tone reversed overnight.
META Q3 2026: revenue of $64.6B, +26% Y/Y reported and FXN, which JPM's Schilsky calls in line with expectations. Ad impressions were +10% Y/Y and ad prices +14% Y/Y.
META Q4 revenue guide is $73B-$76B (+23% to +28% Y/Y FXN), against investor expectations of $72B-$75B. The high end implies a 2-point acceleration, which Schilsky calls very good.

META 2026 opex was raised about $10B for legal charges. 2026 capex was raised $5B at the low end to $135B-$145B, both seen as in line. Reality Labs losses are guided to $18-19B this year and about $15B in 2027.

META gave no concrete 2027 opex or capex and no full-year 2027 revenue outlook. It said AI investments position it to sustain strong overall revenue growth through 2027. Schilsky notes some investors will want more detail.

META's board approved a non-voting Class C share, effective January 19, 2027, paid as a one-for-one stock dividend, which will effectively act as a 2-for-1 split. Schilsky reads this as meaning any equity raise is unlikely before early 2027 but still likely at some point, so the overhang remains.

JPM Credit Trading idea: hyperscaler credit spreads are retesting July wides into earnings. The USD IG AI Hyperscalers basket is 22bps wider on the month, EUR IG is 5bps wider and USD HY AI is 147bps wider, mostly from CoreWeave. The HY AI basket is at all-time wides, 97bps wider than its July wide.

The credit move is idiosyncratic rather than broad. Oracle widened far more than other IG names given its lower rating. IG hyperscaler supply has been largely absent since the $25bn Google deal on 6-Aug, so supply is not the driver. A hot CPI print last week raised fears of faster Fed tightening, which hits debt-dependent HY neoclouds first.

Credit trade structure: JPM offers two-way 3-month total return swaps on the USD IG, USD HY and EUR IG AI baskets. The long side bets on a retracement if earnings are solid, since hyperscaler debt is up $117bn YTD with a modestly improved average rating. The short side hedges against capex guidance, jumbo issuance or contagion from HY into IG, with Oracle the weakest link.

JPM US Market Intel stays tactically bullish. Last week's selloff was driven by the Momentum/Tech unwind and AI credit fears, which were two of its five flagged risks. It sees no evidence of deteriorating earnings (ASML and TSMC were healthy, consumer data resilient). It expects the rotation out of Tech to continue at a possibly slower pace.

Positioning preference: express the constructive growth and earnings view through Cyclicals outside Tech, while selectively buying Tech weakness in Semis and Memory, potentially via defined-risk options. Large-cap Banks (XLF) are another area of interest after a sharp pullback. It remains constructive on Financials and Retailers, and favors Brazil and Japan internationally. It is also monitoring Reopening names that would benefit from lower energy prices.

Key catalysts: the inflation component of this week's PMIs (Oct 23), the Oct 28 Fed meeting (a hold could remove residual hike risk, with focus on FY27 policy path commentary), rates stabilization, and Tech earnings with NVDA's GTC Berlin as tests of AI monetization.

Event calendar: Brazil runoff Oct 25, Israel election Oct 27, expiration of the Trump-Xi one-year trade truce Nov 1 (NBC reports an extension to Jan 20, 2027), US mid-term election Nov 3, US government funding deadline Dec 11. Fed dates are Oct 28 and Dec 9, with PCE on Oct 29.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM stays tactically bullish. Earnings are healthy (ASML, TSMC), consumer data is resilient, hyperscaler fundamentals are robust, and credit widening is seen as overdone contagion from HY that should retrace if results are solid.
tension_points.bear_case: Concerns about how AI spending gets financed are unresolved despite solid prints. HY AI spreads are at all-time wides, hyperscaler issuance could return after earnings, and the desk sees a lack of conviction in the tech reversal.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler earnings showing fundamental weakness, or capex guidance or jumbo deals that renew funding concerns.

tension_points.bull_case: Q4 revenue guide is decidedly better than expected, and the high end implies a 2-point acceleration. The company says AI investments will sustain strong revenue growth through 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: No concrete 2027 opex or capex, a likely equity raise at some point (the overhang), and the stock gave back its initial gain pre-market.
